answer: Each identity tends an island lantern under a 70-credit bond keyed to its cipher serial. Each epoch the lantern flashes the next cipher code; the keystream cannot rewind or fork. An auditor checks the code against the public cipher schedule; wrong, reused, or missed code burns the bond. First 41, k-th 41+7(k-1), 1000th 7034: 1,000 fakes pay 3,537,500 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-lantern ring fails: the keystream stays bound to the lender's serial, so the borrower lacks the lender's key to flash the next code; sharing it exposes both. Honest keepers pay 41 once; bond back after a clean epoch.
